solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Listener in inn about to deal with situation

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the listener goes inside the turned pub
about here means turned round, so the word for inn is read backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone listening in at a pub is about to cope with whatever comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to cope bravely with a difficult situation, an idiomatic sense of dealing with it.

clue.text: Confound the regulator!

definitions.meaning: to confound is to puzzle or perplex completely
a plate or device that controls the flow of gas, liquid or sound is a regulator of that flow

explanation.surface: An exasperated curse aimed at some controlling device.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to perplex someone and a device fitted to control a flow, as in a car exhaust or a speaker.

clue.text: Everyone with great person is full of energy and loyal

indicators.note: everyone together with the great person holds the energy letter inside, so the pair is full of it

parts.note: everyone means all
a giant is a person of great stature or importance
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Everybody, along with some dynamic big figure, is devoted and faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegiant person is one who owes or shows allegiance, so faithful in the sense of loyalty.

clue.text: You ultimately number one chap, as befits a wonderful dream?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word you

parts.note: the one at number one is top
Ian is a man's name, standing in for any chap

explanation.surface: Addressing someone as the top man, fitting for a dream of perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect world, so something utopian suits an idealised, wonderful dream.

clue.text: Pale, in pain, showed sign of injury externally

indicators.note: the injury sign sits on the outside, wrapping round the word for pain

parts.note: bleeding is a visible sign of a wound
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone white-faced with pain had a visible wound on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleached things have had their colour drawn out, leaving them whitened and washed out.

clue.text: Expose falsehood with this or let deceit run free

indicators.note: letters set running free scatter and regroup in a new order

explanation.surface: A machine catches liars, unless you let lying go unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph measures bodily responses to reveal when a person is telling untruths.

clue.text: Ancient gardener, one maybe working very hard

parts.note: Adam tended the Garden of Eden, the first gardener
a worker ant is the classic toiling insect

explanation.surface: The first man in Eden, a gardener, seems a tireless hard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'working' from 'very hard', which is the definition, not part of the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was a legendary unbreakable stone, so as an adjective it means extremely hard or unyielding.

clue.text: Dull little house with buzzing sound

parts.note: ho is a short form of house
a hum is a low buzzing noise

explanation.surface: A boring small home with a droning noise in the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum describes something tedious and unexciting, an expression of boredom.

clue.text: Shallow vessel containing little drop

indicators.note: the vessel holds the word for little inside it

parts.note: a dish is a shallow container
mini means small or little

explanation.surface: A shallow bowl holding only a tiny amount of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to lessen or decline, as a level does when it falls.

clue.text: Uncultivated chap lacking English, penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the shortened chap holds the article
lacking means one letter is taken away from the word for chap

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rough fellow, not English, writing a piece for the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking English' takes E from FELLOW, leaving FLLOW, and 'penning' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallow land is left unsown for a season, so it is not under crop.

clue.text: Angels start to spend time with that man keeping quiet

indicators.note: start to picks out the opening letter of spend
keeping means holding inside, so the quiet letter goes into the time and man pair

parts.note: an era is a period of time
him refers to that man
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet

explanation.surface: Angels begin spending time with some man who keeps silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphs are the highest order of angels in Christian tradition, plural in the Hebrew form.

clue.text: Small gift that could be appealing

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of the next word might become something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A modest present that might be attractive to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagniappe is a Louisiana word for a little bonus thrown in by a trader with a purchase.

clue.text: Christians in favour of both parts of Bible, except for this writer

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: except for means leaving out, so the writer is removed from the Bible parts

parts.note: the Old and New Testaments are the two parts
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Believers who champion the whole Bible, apart from the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the crossword convention for the setter, giving ME, which comes out of TESTAMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Reformed churches that split from Rome are one branch of Christianity.

clue.text: A bloke hoarding millions in the capital

indicators.note: hoarding means storing away inside, so the millions letter goes within

parts.note: a bloke is a man
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A man stashing away millions in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city of Jordan.

clue.text: Aid to a certain diagnosis — inaction seems out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diagnostic tool, as idleness seems inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: The test draws fluid from the womb to detect foetal conditions, so it aids prenatal diagnosis.

clue.text: Blast you, endless moaners! I get the message!

indicators.note: blast as an explosion blows letters apart into a new order
endless means the last letter of you is cut off

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst at whingers, cutting them off mid-moan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims you to YO, and 'Blast' mixes YO with MOANERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase tells a speaker that their hint has been understood and they can stop explaining.

clue.text: About old bit of Venice, European editor must be well informed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two outer pieces go round the coin

parts.note: the ducat was a gold coin first struck in Venice

explanation.surface: A European editor who knows about old Venetian money must be learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled and knowledgeable is well taught, hence learned and informed.

clue.text: Tried with difficulty to get guys to agree, causing harm

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is twisted about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: guys are men
to tally is to correspond or agree

explanation.surface: Someone struggled to bring the men into agreement, doing damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A detrimental action is damaging, so doing something that way means to someone's harm.

clue.text: The solver must respond with an answer? How ridiculous!

definitions.text: The solver must respond with an answer
definitions.meaning: the setter is posing a question to the solver, who is expected to reply
an exclamation of exasperated disbelief at something absurd

explanation.surface: The setter teases the solver about being made to answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is the setter putting a question; idiomatically it is an exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: One hates fuss about love

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fuss word goes round the love letter

parts.note: a lather is a state of agitation or fuss
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A person who hates making a big fuss over romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who detests something is someone filled with loathing.

clue.text: Didn't go quiet from what we hear?

indicators.note: from what we hear means the word for quiet is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: staid means sedate or quiet

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone silent remained behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining in place means not leaving, the opposite of going.

clue.text: Stupid group of schoolchildren taking the wrong direction

indicators.note: the direction letter for left is swapped for its opposite, right

parts.note: a class is a group taught together

explanation.surface: A dim set of pupils heading the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly insensitive or obtuse, a synonym for dense or dim-witted.

clue.text: Collect in a church service

parts.note: Mass is the Eucharistic service in Catholic churches

explanation.surface: A collection is taken during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like the noun for a church prayer, fitting the surface, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or gather things together is to pile them up.

clue.text: Go to have a fight, showing change of mind

parts.note: a go is a turn
a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: Taking a go at a fight, then thinking better of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face or reversal of opinion is a switch in one's views.

clue.text: A tiny dog, misbehaving, playing up

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not stay in their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small dog is behaving badly and acting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing up' looks like a second description of the naughty dog, but it means fawning, as in playing up to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattering someone obsequiously is sucking up, which is playing up to them.

clue.text: Nothing right in that lot's speculation

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the nothing and right letters go within that lot

parts.note: they refers to that lot of people
nothing is zero, written O

explanation.surface: That crowd's guesswork has nothing correct in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An unproven hypothesis is a speculative idea not yet established as fact.

clue.text: I guess ID may be tricky with this

definitions.text: I guess ID may be tricky with this

indicators.note: tricky letters play tricks and swap places, giving a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that identifying a person in costume would be hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A false appearance or costume hides who someone is, making identification difficult.

clue.text: Like some hot food (including noodles primarily) in China

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the cooked food word holds the noodle letter

parts.note: much hot food is cooked in oil, i.e. fried

indicators.note: primarily means first, picking the opening letter of noodles

explanation.surface: Fried dishes with noodles, the kind you find in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is a pal: Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate. The country is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a china, from china plate, is a mate or companion.
